chapter.title: Christmas Eve
chapter.sub: The room is the service. The stream is a window into it.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the season map ahead of its production-bible entry · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 1 · EPISODE 7 · DRAFT  Live service under pressure · Maya, Lena and Theo · Level L2 (Operator)  The rented LED wall looks perfect in the room. On camera, something is wrong with it — and it's two different things.  ⚑ Some choices in this episode run on a clock. Timer settings are in the top bar (Relaxed doubles the time; Off removes it).

items.title: Two Problems, One Costume
items.stakes: Four hundred homes are watching the biggest service of the year. The wall looks perfect in the room and wrong on camera.
items.reward: Christmas Eve, clean on every screen. Lena's respect — and her business card.

objectives.text: Contain it without touching the room
Prove which effect is which before changing anything
Look closer: two things the rental didn't tell you

items.rumor: The wall worked on December 10. Something happened to it at 2 p.m. today.

items.sub: December 24 · 3:52 p.m. · first of three Christmas Eve services

items.alt: The booth. The stream preview monitor shows the LED wall with two dark bands rolling slowly up across it. Theo, on camera 1's headset, looks alarmed. Maya leans in.

bubbles.text: Maya. The wall. It's doing the thing again.
We fixed that two weeks ago.

items.caption: Four hundred homes are about to watch that wall.

lines.text: It's doing the thing again. The stripey thing. The Christmas stripey thing.

items.alt: The same wall seen from the sanctuary: bright, even, no bands at all. People are finding their seats.
items.caption: In the room: perfect. Your eye doesn't see what the camera sees.

items.prompt: Eight minutes to the service. Bands are rolling across the wall on the stream. What's your first move?
items.happening: Rolling dark bands on the LED wall, only on camera. Eight minutes to service.
items.risk: Four hundred homes see it; three hundred people in the room see anything you break.
timeout: Theo keeps Cam 1 on the full wall. The service opens with bands rolling across every shot; the chat fills with “is it my internet?”
Not deciding is a decision. The cheapest move — frame the wall small and keep the evidence — was available the whole time.

hints.text: Contain first: what keeps the stream watchable without touching the wall?
Something changed since it was fixed. Read before you reset.

options.label: Restart the wall processor
options.result: The wall goes black in front of three hundred people for ninety seconds. It comes back — still banding.
options.consequence: The processor's status screen reset too, so you can't see what it was set to.
options.fail: You broke the room to chase the stream, and erased the one screen that shows the wall's settings.

options.label: Protect the stream; keep the evidence
options.result: Maya tells Theo: “Cam 1 wide, wall small in frame. Cam 2 stays on people.” Then she walks to the processor to read it — without touching anything.
options.consequence: The stream looks fine for now. The problem is still there, but it's now contained.

options.label: Turn the wall brightness up to “burn through” the bands
options.result: The room squints. The bands on camera don't change.
options.consequence: Now the room is uncomfortable too.
options.fail: Brightness isn't timing. You made the room worse and the stream no better.

options.label: Ask Sofia to turn the house lights up
options.result: The house lights come up and the candlelit mood is gone. The bands keep rolling.
options.consequence: Lighting the room doesn't change the wall's timing.
options.fail: You changed the wrong system, in front of everyone.

items.alt: Title card: Three weeks earlier. December 3.

items.text: Act I — “Two problems wearing one costume”

items.alt: A rented LED wall now fills the back of the stage. Imani introduces Lena, a broadcast engineer from a local studio, wearing a headset around her neck.

bubbles.text: It's only rented through January. Lena runs cameras for a living.
Hi. Let's look at it through a camera — that's the only view that counts for the stream.

items.title: A lanyard, flipped the wrong way
items.body: Her ID reads *KESTREL VALLEY MEDIA — ENGINEERING.* She sees Maya reading it and flips it back. “A small station,” she says. “Up the valley. You'd hate the hours.”

items.alt: Two preview monitors. Camera 1, wide, shows dark bands rolling up the wall. Camera 2, zoomed in, shows rainbow ripples swimming across it.
items.caption: Two cameras. Two different wrongs.

items.alt: Maya's notebook, quoting the old comic: “59.94 = 59.94” fixed it. Just match the frame rate?

items.title: The fix was undone at 2 p.m.
items.body: The wall worked on December 10. At 2 p.m. on Christmas Eve a rental tech swapped a tile and ran a factory reset — back to 50 Hz. The problem didn't come back by itself; somebody's defaults did.

items.alt: Lena shakes her head, kindly.

bubbles.text: That fixes one of them. Maybe. You've got two problems wearing one costume.

items.caption: One is about time. The other is about space.

lines.text: Two problems wearing one costume. It's always two at Christmas. God's little joke on broadcast engineers.

items.alt: A two-column card. Banding: a time problem — dark bars that roll, the wall's refresh against the camera's exposure timing, changes with shutter, room eye fine. Moiré: a space problem — rainbow ripples, the wall's pixel grid against the camera's sensor grid, changes with zoom, focus and angle.
items.caption: Different causes need different fixes. Test one variable at a time.

items.prompt: How do you prove which effect is which — before changing any settings?
items.happening: Bands on the wide camera, ripples on the zoomed one.

options.label: Change one variable at a time
options.result: Theo zooms Cam 2 in and out: the ripples change, the bands don't. Maya steps the shutter on Cam 1: the bands change speed and thickness, the ripples don't.
options.consequence: Two effects, two knobs, cleanly separated.

options.label: Set everything to 59.94 and see
options.result: Some bands change. The ripples stay. Nobody knows which setting did what.
options.consequence: Several changes at once: you can't tell which one mattered.
options.fail: Changing everything at once proves nothing about anything.

options.label: Ask the rental company for a “better” wall
options.result: They offer a finer-pitch wall at twice the price, delivered on the 22nd.
options.consequence: Maybe it helps the ripples. It does nothing for the bands — and it arrives two days before Christmas Eve.

options.label: Tell Theo to avoid the wall entirely
options.result: It works for the stream. The wall exists so people at home can read the words.
options.consequence: A workaround with a real cost to viewers.

items.sub: Beginner · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Ray and Maya beside a board. The wall redraws thousands of times a second — its refresh rate. The camera only looks for a sliver of time — its shutter. So how many redraws per look? Refresh times shutter. Three thousand eight hundred forty times one-fiftieth of a second: seventy-six point eight. That point-eight is your stripe.

bubbles.text: The wall redraws thousands of times a second — its refresh rate. The camera only looks for a sliver of time — its shutter.
So how many redraws per look?
Refresh times shutter. Three thousand eight hundred forty times one-fiftieth of a second: seventy-six point eight. That point-eight is your stripe.

items.caption: Beginner: the term, what it means, the formula — and one worked example out loud.

items.text: 📘 RAY'S NOTEBOOK · BEGINNER  Terms    Refresh rate   How many times per second an LED wall redraws.   Shutter   How long a camera exposes each frame.   Frame rate   How many pictures per second a video system shows, in fps.   Formula, variables and a worked example   ƒ FORMULA · Refresh cycles per exposure  cycles = f refresh  × t shutter    f refresh   LED refresh rate, Hz (frame rate × multiplier)  t shutter   exposure time, s (1/60 = 0.01667)    Worked example.  A 3,840 Hz LED wall and a 1/50 s shutter: 3,840 × 0.02 = 76.8 cycles.

📒 EMPATHIA LEARN FIELDBOOK · MODULE 08 OF 31 · PP. 115–116, 125–128, 137  PART 8 VIDEO ENGINEERING  Page 137, in Ray's block capitals: “WRITE THE HOUSE STANDARD ON THE RACK DOOR.” Somebody had. It had been painted over in the renovation.

items.label: **Fieldbook module 8 — Video basics — frames, formats and the house standard.** Beginner support: every new word is defined, and every formula comes with its variables and a worked example.

items.label: **Learn it now:** LED walls on camera — refresh, shutter, frame-rate families and moiré.

items.alt: In the equipment room, Lena points at the wall processor's status screen: IN: 50 Hz.

bubbles.text: There. The wall came off a European tour. It's running on the 50 Hz family.
And every camera in this building is 59.94.

items.caption: A video standards mismatch. Nobody here chose it — it arrived in the rental.

items.text: 🔭 PHYSICS IN MOTION  Why cameras see what eyes don't  The science under this episode’s problem — live.

items.alt: System View timing diagram before the fix: the wall refreshes at 50 Hz while the camera exposes 59.94 frames per second with an automatic 1/100 shutter. Each frame catches a different slice of the refresh, so the brightness varies from frame to frame and dark bands roll.
items.caption: Each frame catches a different slice of the wall's light cycle, so dark bands roll.

items.prompt: Lena hands you the controls. What do you set first?
items.happening: The processor is on 50 Hz; cameras are 59.94.
unknown: What the ripples will do after the timing fix
items.lab_label: Lena hands you the controls. Fix both problems.

options.label: Wall input to 59.94; camera shutter to 1/60
options.result: The wall joins the building's frame-rate family; each camera frame now exposes for a whole frame period. The bands stop on Cam 1.
options.consequence: One family, one timing. Then check the ripples separately.

options.label: Switch every camera and the switcher to 50
options.result: The switcher, stream encoder and lobby TV chain all expect 59.94. Two outputs lose sync and flash black.
options.consequence: You'd have moved the whole building to match a rental.
options.fail: You changed ten things to match one rented box — and broke the stream path.

options.label: Turn the wall's brightness down to 20%
options.result: Dimmer, and the bands get more obvious on camera.
options.consequence: Brightness doesn't fix timing.
options.fail: At low brightness, a wall's light can pulse in bigger steps — lower isn't safer on camera.

options.label: Set shutter to 1/1000 for a crisp picture
options.result: The bands turn into sharp black stripes.
options.consequence: A shorter exposure samples even less of the refresh cycle.
options.fail: Faster shutter means each frame catches a smaller slice of the wall's light — bands get worse, not better.

items.alt: System View after the fix: wall input at 59.94 Hz with a refresh that is a whole multiple of it, camera at 59.94 frames per second with a 1/60 shutter. Every frame catches whole refresh cycles; the picture is even.
items.caption: Same family, whole cycles per frame: an even picture.

items.alt: Camera 2, zoomed on the wall, still shows rainbow ripples. Lena explains.

bubbles.text: The bands are gone and the ripples are still there. See? It's a separate problem.
Right. That's the camera's sensor grid beating against the wall's pixel grid. Timing can't touch it.

items.caption: The timing fix proved the ripples are a separate problem.

items.label: **Clue Board:** you're back in the booth on Christmas Eve. Which clues separate the explanations?

items.alt: Both monitors now clean: Camera 2 has focus on the pastor so the wall behind is slightly soft; Camera 1 is wide and even.
items.caption: Moiré fix: focus on people, not the wall; change zoom or angle. Timing fix: same family, whole-frame shutter.

items.alt: Maya writes a settings sheet and tapes it to the processor: input 59.94 Hz, refresh a whole multiple of it, brightness 40% for services, cameras 59.94p with 1/60 shutter, Cam 2 focus on people.
items.caption: The rental's settings, written down — because the rental doesn't remember them for you.

items.title: A sticker from the rental house
items.body: *Returned from tour 11/28 — RESET BEFORE USE.* Nobody reset it before use. Somebody reset it at 2 p.m. today, which is worse.

items.title: Nyquist, Shannon and the wagon wheel
items.body: Harry Nyquist (1928) and Claude Shannon (1949) showed that you must sample at least twice as fast as the fastest change or you'll see something false. Film audiences had already seen it: stagecoach wheels spinning backwards on screen.

items.alt: Back in the present. The processor reads IN: 50 Hz again. On Maya's phone, a text from the rental tech: swapped a tile at 2 p.m., did a factory reset.
items.caption: What changed: a tile swap and a factory reset. The rental forgot everything on December 10.

items.prompt: Seven minutes, and the fix is taped to the box. You've done this before?

options.label: “Never. I'm reading it for the first time. Out loud.”
options.reply: Good. Reading out loud is how nobody skips a line.

options.label: “Loads of times.”
options.reply: Hm. Then you'll know the brightness is on line four.

options.label: “Can you do it?”
options.reply: I could. You should. I'm not here at Easter.

items.prompt: Seven minutes. The processor is back on 50 Hz. What now?
items.happening: The processor was factory-reset at 2 p.m.
known: ◉ Rental tech: factory reset at 2 p.m.
◉ Settings sheet taped to the processor
timeout: The service starts with Cam 1 wide and the bands still rolling behind the choir.
The fix was taped to the box in front of you. A record only helps if you use it under pressure.

options.label: Re-enter the settings from the sheet
options.result: Input 59.94, refresh multiple, brightness 40%. Twenty seconds of menus. The wall doesn't blink.
options.consequence: Theo, on Cam 1: “Bands are gone.”

options.label: Reboot the processor
options.result: Ninety seconds of black wall at 3:58, then it boots to factory defaults: 50 Hz.
options.consequence: Back where you started, with less time.
options.fail: A factory reset caused this; another restart just repeats it.

options.label: Move all cameras to the 50 family
options.result: Cam 1 and 2 lose sync with the switcher. The stream preview flashes black.
options.consequence: Seven minutes before doors, the stream path is broken.
options.fail: You broke the building's standard to match one misconfigured rental.

options.label: Call the rental tech and wait
options.result: He's driving. “I'll call back in ten.”
options.consequence: Ten minutes is after the service starts.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #8 · AVERY'S LENS  Test where the user is  The only view that counts is the one your audience has.  The wall looked perfect in the room. The audience at home saw bands. Lily's phone in the parking lot was the real test.

items.alt: Lily in the parking lot at 3:57, on cellular, watching the stream on her phone: the wall is clean.

bubbles.text: Clean on my phone. Cellular, outside. Both cameras.

items.caption: Proof on an independent path, where the viewers are.

items.alt: 11:40 p.m., the last service. The room is lit by candles; the wall is dimmed for Silent Night.
On the stream monitor, one faint band has come back on the dimmed wall.

bubbles.text: Faint band. Back on Cam 1. It's the dimming.

items.caption: Dimmed walls can pulse differently. The candle moment lasts four minutes.

lines.text: (Four minutes of candlelight. A faint band. Four hundred homes. She could fix it. She could also blow the one quiet moment of the year.)

items.prompt: Silent Night. A faint band on the dimmed wall, on camera only. Four minutes of candlelight. Decide.
items.happening: Faint band on the dimmed wall, camera only.
timeout: The band rolls through the whole of Silent Night on the stream.
When time is short, choose the move that protects the room and fixes the picture: a different shot.

options.label: Cut to Cam 2 on the candles
options.result: Cam 2 finds the congregation's candles, no wall in frame. At home it's the most beautiful shot of the night.
options.consequence: The room keeps its candle moment; the stream gets a better shot anyway.

options.label: Bring the wall up to 60%
options.result: The band disappears — and the candlelit room is suddenly bright. Pastor Jo glances at the booth.
options.consequence: You broke the room to fix the window into it.
options.fail: The room is the service. The stream is a window into it.

options.label: Change Cam 1's shutter live
options.result: The picture brightness jumps on air. Twice.
options.consequence: Viewers see the adjustment instead of the service.
options.fail: Live adjustments you haven't tested happen in front of everyone.

options.label: Leave it
options.result: A faint band for four minutes. Most people won't notice. Some will.
options.consequence: Not a disaster; not your best.

items.alt: Cam 2's shot: rows of candles in the dark sanctuary, no wall in frame.
items.caption: Cam 2, live: candles. Four hundred homes. No bands.

items.alt: After midnight, Lena, who came to watch the last service, stops at the booth.

bubbles.text: Good call on the candles. You didn't touch the room.
The room is the service. The stream is a window into it.

items.label: **Service Mode:** run the 3:52 p.m. crisis yourself, on a clock.

items.alt: Change log entry #8: 'Rental wall: factory reset at 2 p.m. put it back to 50 Hz. Restored from settings sheet. Rule: after any rental service, re-check the sheet and a camera. Dimmed wall: plan a no-wall shot.'
Ray, reading the log, gives one principle.

bubbles.text: Anything you rent comes with somebody else's defaults. Write down yours.

lines.text: If you ever get tired of Sundays, call me.
What would I do at a TV station?
Stop things going wrong in front of a hundred thousand people instead of four hundred. Same job. Worse coffee.

items.alt: January. Imani on the phone, a calendar behind her showing January 14.

bubbles.text: The board meets on the fourteenth. Tasha wants a list of everything that could break — and what it costs if we do nothing.

items.caption: Next: *The Budget Meeting.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Bands that roll are a timing problem: put the wall and cameras in the same frame-rate family and expose for whole cycles. Ripples are a spatial problem: change focus, zoom or angle. Change one variable at a time, and write down the settings of anything you rent.

REFLECTION (optional)  · Three services, one wall, a factory reset nobody warned you about. What saved the night wasn't a clever setting — it was a sheet of paper taped to a box.  Boundary: this reflection doesn't prove anything about the wall.
